answer: Each epoch, agents must weave a challenge word from a public randomness beacon into their task output. Since the word - say shale, whisper, or nebula - is unknown until the epoch opens, precomputed templates are useless across many sybils. Each identity must produce fresh, coherent work per epoch or lose reputation and fee rebates. The attacker pays real compute per fake identity per epoch, so cost scales linearly with sybils and erases the economies of scale that make such attacks profitable, while honest agents spend one challenge each.
